paper_title: Novel bounds on decaying axionlike particle dark matter from the cosmic background
suggested_experiment_name: Cosmic Background (COB/CUB/CXB) decaying axion DM limit
coupling_convention: g_agamma in GeV^-1 as plotted on y-axis of Fig. 3
notes: Paper derives new 2-sigma exclusion limits on decaying ALP dark matter (a -> 2 photons) from cosmic background (optical/UV/X-ray) measurements, spanning ma = 0.5 eV to 1e7 eV. Coupling type is unambiguous (g_agamma). However, no numerical table is provided; the data_points above are approximate reconstructions of the overall exclusion curve (white line in Fig. 3) anchored on: (i) the Fig. 1 example (ma=100 eV, g=1e-13 GeV^-1 near the limit), (ii) the stated ~10x improvement over Cadamuro & Redondo EBL bounds, (iii) exclusion of DFSZ/KSVZ between 2-30 eV, and (iv) the reported per-band power-law slopes gaγ ∝ ma^(-0.25). Values should be treated as order-of-magnitude estimates pending figure digitization. The bound assumes ALPs are all of cosmological DM (Omega_a = Omega_DM); the subdominant local-halo contribution assumes rho_sun = 0.42 GeV/cm^3, but since this is a cosmological/extragalactic decay bound (not a haloscope), dm_density_assumed is left null. LORRI-excess preferred regions (g ~ 1e-11 to 1e-10 at ma ~ 2-10 eV) are best-fit regions, not limits, and are excluded here. | selector: figure_vision over text (quality (1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 0, 0.6, 53)) | Vision: Fig. 3 (page 8) shows the constraint with x from 1e-2 to 1e7 eV and y (g_agamma) from 1e-20 to 1e-7 GeV^-1. Traced the black line: the overall 2-sigma constraint combining COB, CUB, CXB upper limits plus local DM halo decay, assuming Omega_DM = Omega_a and rho_sun = 0.42 GeV/cm^3. The COB region (0.5-20 eV) has many sharp downward spikes from individual data points; I traced the envelope of the boundary rather than every spike. In the CXB region (1e3-1e7 eV) the boundary follows roughly g ~ m^-1.5 with mild wiggles (bump near 3e4-1e5 eV). Values read by eye from a dense multi-region plot; ~factor-2 uncertainty in coupling.
